corpusA.desc: 4 arXiv papers: Transformer, BERT, Sentence-BERT, RAG (11–19 pages each)

corpusB.desc: 2 long arXiv papers: GPT-3 (75 pages) and Llama 2 (77 pages)

notes: Full evidence retrieved: A 7 → 8 of 10, B 2 → 5 of 6 answerable questions
Long documents gain most from a larger top-k
Persistent misses: F3 (wording mismatch) and a cross-document comparison (LM2)
retrieval.speaker: Bars show the share of answerable questions whose full evidence was in the retrieved chunks, judged from the chunk text (final V1.1 runs; A n=10, B n=6). Small samples: one question is 10 to 17 points. F3's evidence ranks 22nd for its wording but 1st when the question says 'Wikipedia dump'.

quality.abstainLabel: unanswerable responses correctly abstained (5 questions × 2 settings)
quality.note: False premises: never corrected; abstained in 5 of 6 responses, fabricated once (A2 at top-k 8). More context did not always help the 3B model.
quality.speaker: Judged outcomes for answerable questions in the final runs. Top-k 8 retrieves more evidence but corpus A correct answers went 7 to 6, latency roughly doubled (7 s to 13 s), and the only hallucination appeared at top-k 8. These are draft judgements to be confirmed; see docs/evaluation_report.md.

failures.title: F3: RAG's Wikipedia index
failures.what: The evidence on p. 4 ranks 22nd: the question says 'non-parametric memory', the passage says 'Wikipedia dump', and the chunk mixes two sections.
failures.status: Unresolved. Chunk sizes and a second embedding model didn't fix it; hybrid BM25 or a reranker is next.

failures.title: BLEU 38.1 vs 28.4
failures.what: Table 2 is flattened into bare numbers; 38.1 is the base model's EN-FR score, read from the wrong row and column.
failures.status: Mitigated: rule 9. No wrong number in 8 test phrasings; one phrasing now abstains instead.

failures.title: A2: false premise
failures.what: 'Why does SBERT use [CLS] by default?' (it uses MEAN). The model justified the premise from BERT passages.
failures.status: Partly fixed: rule 10 makes top-k 4 abstain; top-k 8 still fabricates.

failuresSpeaker: Each failure was root-caused before any change. Only prompt-level fixes were made; their verification is limited to the tested questions with llama3.2:3b at temperature 0.
limitations: No OCR: scanned PDFs are rejected with an explanation
Tables and figures lose structure in text extraction
Dense retrieval misses passages worded differently from the question
3B local model: occasional omissions, contradictions and one fabrication
Single-user local prototype; 24-question evaluation, one run per setting
improvements: Hybrid BM25 + dense search, or a cross-encoder reranker (F3, LM2, premise chunks)
Stronger LLM via the existing OpenAI-compatible setting (S2, M2, A2)
Table-aware extraction for numeric questions (BLEU case)
conclusion: A working local RAG chatbot that cites file and page and abstained on every unanswerable test question. Evaluation shows retrieval is the main bottleneck, with false premises the main hallucination risk.
